text: If you go into space without a suit, you don't explode. That's the bad news. With no air pressure, the water in your body starts to boil, even at body temperature. Your skin swells, but it holds. You'd have about ten to fifteen seconds before you pass out. In 1966, a NASA test subject's suit leaked in a vacuum chamber. The last thing he remembered was the saliva on his tongue starting to bubble. They re-pressurised in seconds and he survived. Dave: still not exploded. Just disappointed.
